items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Monday directed the State to constitute a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to investigate into irregularities in the recruitment of veterinary doctors and several other posts by the Karnataka State Public Commission (KPSC) [Raj Mohammed v. State of Karnataka]. Justice M Nagaprasanna ordered the formation of the SIT without transferring the matter from the State Crime Investigation Department (CID) to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). Reasoning that the CBI has previously taken considerable time to conclude investigation, the Court emphasised on the urgency of restoring the sanctity of the constitutional promises of merit and equality. "Every passing month may leave hundreds of aspirants suspended between hope and uncertainty; age limits may overtake some, other opportunities may disappear for others, and an entire recruitment may remain frozen in litigation. Justice to job aspirants cannot be rendered, after their opportunity itself has withered away," the Court said. items.title: "Wild witch hunt": Delhi High Court rejects plea for CBI probe into Justice Yashwant Varma episode
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Monday refused to entertain a plea seeking registration of a first information report (FIR) and a probe by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) or a Special Investigation Team (SIT) in the Justice Yashwant Varma case. Justice Amit Bansal questioned the locus of the petitioner, Advocate Ghanshyam Upadhyay, and said that he had an alternate remedy to approach the Delhi Police and then the competent magistrate. "I am not entertaining this sir. This is a wild witch hunt. You have nothing better to do?" the Court remarked. Upadhyaya had appeared in person before the Court and argued that the matter is of "extraordinary nature" and that a magistrate will not be competent to do justice with it. "He [magistrate] cannot direct the CBI or SIT inquiry. Magistrate or special court will not be competent to deal with the matter," Upadhyay said. Central Government Standing Counsel (CGSC) Premtosh Kumar Mishra appeared for the Union of India and the CBI and said that Upadhyay had earlier approached the Supreme Court and the top court rejected his plea. items.title: Delhi court sets aside order refusing FIR against Sonia Gandhi over voter roll inclusion; orders fresh hearing
items.summary: A Delhi sessions court on Monday set aside a magistrate's refusal to order the registration of an FIR against Congress leader Sonia Gandhi over the alleged inclusion of her name in the electoral roll before she became an Indian citizen. Judge Visha Gogne set aside the magistrate court order of September 2025 and directed that the plea will be heard and decided afresh. The court said that the magistrate must pass a reasoned order after hearing the complainant, Vikas Tripathi, and the Delhi Police. In a detailed order pronounced in court, Judge Gogne ruled that the trial court order was perverse and improper. The sessions court said that the magistrate's order was non speaking on the question of disclosure of a cognizable offence against Sonia Gandhi. "It suffers from manifest error in law on account of non-compliance with BNSS provisions, inter alia, not calling for a status report of the hearing submission from the police," the sessions court said. It also observed that the sanctity of the electoral roll is an article of faith for every citizen in a parliamentary democracy and that even the "mightiest" in the land are voters like ordinary citizens. items.title: Bombay High Court initiates suo motu case on festival noise; flags midnight loudspeakers, moots firecracker ban
items.summary: The Bombay High Court has taken suo motu cognizance of severe noise and air pollution caused by loudspeakers, amplifiers and firecrackers during festival celebrations. A division bench of Justices GS Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale expressed deep concern over the ground level failure to implement noise control regulations and initiated a public interest litigation. Justices GS Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale In its order of September 21, the Court noted that public celebrations cannot override constitutional rights. “There cannot be any objection to the festivities/processions being held, however, they need to be held in a manner, which is conducive and cognizant of the rights of the citizens at large, qua the adverse impact created by the high decibel noise pollution,” the bench observed. It underlined that vulnerable persons including ailing senior citizens and students are left suffering. “The celebrations certainly need to take place, but they cannot be at the cost of breach of the legal rights of thousands of citizens, who are seriously and adversely impacted, and who are left to suffer silently, ” the order stated. items.title: Arbitration may rhyme with "arbitrary" but arbitral proceedings can't be arbitrary: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently quipped that though the word "arbitration" rhymes with "arbitrary", arbitral proceedings cannot be conducted in an arbitrary or biased manner [ Arth Micro Finance Private Ltd & Ors. v. Shivalik Small Finance Bank Ltd. ]. In an order passed on September 17, a Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran emphasised that bias and lack of consent render the initiation of arbitration invalid in law. "Arbitration, though rhymes with it, cannot result in an arbitrary measure, even in the appointment of an Arbitral Tribunal," the Court said. Hence, it set aside a High Court order that had dismissed an appeal against three interim directions passed by an arbitral tribunal under Section 17 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice Vinod Chandran The Court was hearing an appeal filed by Arth Micro Finance challenging interim orders passed by an arbitral tribunal appointed at the instance of Shivalik Small Finance Bank. The tribunal had issued directions freezing several bank accounts of Arth, permitting Shivalik to take over movable and immovable properties and ordering the transfer of deposited funds into Shivalik's bank

items.title: Supreme Court rejects Centre's review petition against verdict on private complaints in Companies Act fraud cases
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday dismissed a review petition filed by the Central government against its judgment holding that a special court cannot take cognisance of certain Companies Act offences linked to fraud based on private complaints. [Union of India v. State of Telangana] A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices K Vinod Chandran and Joymalya Bagchi was dealing with the Centre's plea seeking review of the Court's January 9 judgment concerning the bar contained in the second proviso to Section 212(6) of the Companies Act, 2013. CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice Vinod Chandran While declining to reconsider the judgment, the Court clarified that the Central government was at liberty to exercise its powers under the second proviso to Section 212(6) and authorise any officer, by a general or special order in writing, to institute the complaint. The clarification assumes significance since Section 212(6) permits cognisance upon a written complaint by the Director of the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) or an officer of the Central government authorised by a general or special written order. items.title: NCLT, NCLAT are government's lifeline; should have basic facilities: Supreme Court
items.summary: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) and the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) are government's "lifeline", the Supreme Court said on Monday while expressing concern over inadequate infrastructure and shortage of members at NCLT benches across the country. A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said institutions dealing with disputes involving thousands of crores could not be expected to function without basic amenities, adequate staff and technological support. "They are the government's lifeline now. All nationalised banks, banking sector, and all infrastructure projects are also matter of examination before these tribunals only, " the Court said. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The Court was hearing a suo motu case concerning appointment of judicial and technical members and inadequate infrastructure at the NCLT. items.title: Gujarat High Court gives Adani more time to respond to Journalist Ravi Nair's plea against custody in defamation case
items.summary: The Gujarat High Court on Monday adjourned journalist Ravi Nair's plea challenging his custody in a criminal defamation case in which he was convicted earlier this year for allegedly defaming the Adani Group. Nair had been released on bail during the pendency of his appeal against the conviction but was again taken into custody last week following the issuance of a non-bailable warrant against him by the Sessions Court. He has now moved the High Court to seek his release. Justice MK Thakker today granted Adani Enterprises more time to respond to Nair's plea seeking release from judicial custody. Senior counsel Mitesh Amin appearing for Adani submitted that he would like to put on record certain facts which may go against Nair. He thus sought a short date to file a response to Nair's plea. Advocate Abhik Chimni opposed the request, submitting that he was pressing for interim release of Nair. "They have no position to say anything in this matter. A Supreme Court judgment squarely covers me. This is at an appellate stage. This is not even the trial. Why should I even spend one day in jail," Chimni argued. items.title: DHJS officer Reetesh Singh appointed new Registrar General of Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has appointed Delhi Higher Judicial Service (DHJS) officer Reetesh Singh as its new registrar general. At present, Singh is posted as Principal Secretary (Law, Justice and Legislative Affairs), Government of NCT of Delhi. "Hon'ble the Chief Justice has been pleased to appoint Mr. Reetesh Singh, an Officer of Delhi Higher Judicial Service, presently posted as Principal Secretary (Law, Justice and Legislative Affairs), Govt. of NCT of Delhi, as Registrar General in this Court on deputation basis, with effect from 22.09.2026," read a notification issued by the High Court. Singh has been given the assignment after the elevation of the High Court's former registrar general Arun Bhardwaj as an additional judge of the High Court. items.title: Karnataka High Court upholds tax refund of ₹27.13 crore to Myntra and Cult.fit co-founder Mukesh Bansal
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has set aside the revision proceedings initiated by the Income Tax (IT) Department against entrepreneur Mukesh Bansal in relation to a refund of over ₹27.13 crore return for the Assessment Year 2019-2020 [Mukesh Bansal v Principal Commissioner of Income Tax, Bengaluru-2] Justice S Sunil Dutt Yadav held the notice issued to Bansal, who co-founded Myntra, Cult.Fit, and Meraki Labs, for hearing of the revision proceedings was without any jurisdiction and required to be set aside. The Court ruled that the intimation under Section 143(1) could not be treated as an order for the purpose of revision of power under Section 263 of the IT Act. "The treating of an intimation under Section 143(1) as a notice of demand is by a fiction of law which cannot be extended to deeming the passing of an Assessment Order prior to an intimation," the Court said on September 18. Justice Sunil Dutt Yadav Bansal had declared income of ₹231.73 crore for the year 2019-20, tax liability of ₹82.55 crore and claimed a refund of ₹6.07 Lakh. The same was processed.
